description: Labelled dataset for the Phase 7 evaluation harness (`--evaluate`). Ground truth is a single developer's sentence-level judgement: does the sentence contain at least one genuine ambiguity? This is a small, single-annotator dataset - see the README's Phase 7 section and Future Work for that documented limitation. Kept separate from data/examples/adjudication_cases.json, which has no ground-truth label and is for --live-llm-test demos only.

cases.text: She found a bat in the garage.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: 'bat' (baseball equipment vs. the animal) with no disambiguating context; both readings are ordinary.

cases.text: He works at the plant near the river.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: 'plant' (factory vs. a living plant) - a factory reading is more common, but both are available without further context.

cases.text: The detective observed the woman with binoculars.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: PP-attachment: 'with binoculars' can modify 'observed' (instrument) or 'woman' (possession).

cases.text: Old men and women gathered in the square.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: Coordination scope: 'old' may modify only 'men', or both 'men and women'.

cases.text: Sarah told Emily that she had won the award.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: 'she' has two plausible antecedents (Sarah, Emily) surviving number/animacy agreement.

cases.text: The company shipped the packages to the clients before they closed for the holidays.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: 'they' could refer to the company or the clients; both can plausibly 'close for the holidays'.

cases.text: The lawyer informed the client that she needed additional documents.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: 'she' could be the lawyer or the client - both are grammatically and pragmatically available.

cases.text: The fish is ready to cook.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: Tough-construction agent/patient ambiguity: the fish could be about to cook something, or about to be cooked.

cases.text: She is an American history teacher.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: Classic noun-compound ambiguity: a teacher of American history, or an American who teaches history.

cases.text: Every senator didn't vote for the bill.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: Quantifier/negation scope: 'no senator voted for it' vs. 'not every senator voted for it'.

cases.text: All the students didn't pass the test.
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: Same quantifier/negation scope pattern as scope_every_senator, with 'all' instead of 'every'.

cases.text: Could you pass the salt?
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: Literal question about ability vs. a conventional indirect request - the README's own Section 6.6 example pattern.

cases.text: Would you mind closing the door?
cases.label: ambiguous
cases.notes: Literal question about willingness vs. a polite request; a conventional indirect speech act.

cases.text: She deposited her paycheck at the credit union on Main Street.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: No polysemous target word and only one plausible attachment; a lexical/syntactic control.

cases.text: The children played fetch with the golden retriever in the park.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: Ordinary sentence with no structural or lexical ambiguity signal expected.

cases.text: He read the newspaper while waiting for the bus.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: Simple coordination-free sentence; control for false positives on common nouns.

cases.text: The chef sliced the tomatoes for the salad.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: No tough-construction, no unresolved pronoun, no quantifier; a semantic-detector control.

cases.text: After the meeting ended, everyone went home for the evening.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: 'everyone' is a quantifier but there is no negation or second quantifier in the same clause.

cases.text: Three of the ten students failed the final exam.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: Numeric quantifiers with no negation; a scope-detector control.

cases.text: The nurse gave the patient his medication before the surgery started.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: Only one male referent ('the patient') is available for 'his'; a referential-detector control.

cases.text: The teacher explained the assignment clearly to the students.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: Plain declarative sentence with no structural ambiguity signal expected.

cases.text: The committee will announce the winner at the ceremony tomorrow.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: Collective noun with no quantifier or negation; control for the scope detector.

cases.text: The soldiers marched across the bridge at dawn.
cases.label: not_ambiguous
cases.notes: No PP-attachment alternative and no polysemous target word in this usage.
